name: JavaScript core and ES6+
description: Scope, this, prototypes, the event loop, array and object methods, destructuring, optional chaining, fetch and AbortController. Mandatory: closures, promises, async and await, and modules (ES modules).

name: Browser and web fundamentals
description: The DOM, events, rendering, HTTP and HTTPS, how a request travels, and postMessage between a page and an iframe. Mandatory: storage (localStorage, IndexedDB), cookies (including sameSite), CORS (including with credentials) and HTTP caching.

name: React
description: Props, and practice: modals and confirm dialogs, toasts, accordions, drag and drop and long-press select. Mandatory: functional components and hooks only (useState, useEffect, useRef, useMemo), state, effects, routing (React Router, protected routes), forms with validation and performance (memoisation).

name: Node.js
description: Modules in Node (CommonJS and ES modules), the event loop, streams and error handling. Theory only: services and background jobs and an RSS feed proxy with size and time limits. Mandatory: environment settings, and working with files.

name: Express
description: Monolith and microservices (what they are), controllers and services, route-level auth, cookie-parser, helmet, and express-rate-limit behind proxies. Mandatory: routing, middleware, error handling, CORS (with credentials) and validation (input length limits).

name: REST APIs and HTTP
description: Methods, idempotency, pagination, and rewrite rules that serve the API through the frontend's address. Mandatory: status codes (including 409 and 429) and designing endpoints (resource routes).

name: MongoDB
description: The aggregation pipeline, transactions, replication, atomic updates and deleteMany. Mandatory: documents and collections, queries (including queries by owner), indexes (including TTL indexes) and data modelling (references).

name: Mongoose
description: Queries (the query builder), hooks and query performance. Mandatory: schemas and models (learned as logic with your own examples), validation (including field-length validation) and references (populate).

name: Authentication, authorization and security
description: Sessions, XSS, CSRF, NoSQL injection and secrets in environment variables. Mandatory: JWT (access token and refresh token in an httpOnly cookie), bcrypt hashing, email verification and password reset, failed-login lock, role-based access and owner-only resources.

name: Git and GitHub
description: Rebase, stash, reset and resolving conflicts. Mandatory: branches (feature branches), merging (to master) and pull requests.

name: CI/CD and deployment
description: Environments, building images on every merge to master, promoting to production when a version tag is pushed, and re-running transient failures. Mandatory: writing GitHub Actions pipeline files, and deploying to a host (staging first, then production).

name: Docker
description: Containers, volumes, running an app in a container, and pushing the image to the GitHub container registry. Mandatory: Dockerfiles and images.

name: TypeScript
description: Interfaces, generics, strict mode, and typing API responses and hooks. Mandatory: types (typing configuration and data).

name: HTML and CSS
description: Semantic HTML, layout with flexbox and grid, container queries and media queries. Mandatory: responsive design (phone, tablet, desktop).

name: Testing
description: Vitest, what makes a test useful, and testing basics. Mandatory: API tests, and unit tests with Jest.

name: AI tools and calling an AI API
description: Using AI coding tools well, and calling an AI API with structured output.

name: Cloud basics
description: A cloud provider such as AWS, a domain registrar and DNS. Mandatory: hosting, and storage (a media storage service).

name: GraphQL and WebSockets
description: GraphQL queries and schemas, real-time connections with WebSockets, and server-sent events.

name: MQTT basics
description: Publish and subscribe, topics, retained messages, keepalive and reconnect, publishers and listeners, a cloud MQTT broker, and MQTT over WebSocket from the browser.

name: React state management and data fetching
description: Context, Redux basics, and when each fits.

name: File uploads and media storage
description: multer, handling a file upload request, size and dimension checks before upload, resized delivery URLs, and deleting a file together with its record.

name: Web performance
description: Code splitting (including lazy and Suspense), lazy images, idle prefetch, small chunks and Lighthouse basics.

name: Accessibility basics
description: Buttons and labels, aria-expanded, focus handling and keyboard use.

name: SQL and PostgreSQL basics
description: Tables, joins, queries and when a relational database fits better.

name: Linux and the command line
description: Shell commands, files, permissions and processes beyond what Git needs.

name: Tailwind CSS
description: Utility classes and breakpoints.

name: Service workers and offline basics
description: A service worker, the Cache API and serving saved files offline.

name: Kubernetes and Terraform
description: Container orchestration and infrastructure as code.

name: End-to-end testing
description: Browser tests with Playwright or Cypress.

name: Logging and monitoring basics
description: Structured logging. Mandatory: watching an app (a heartbeat with offline detection).

name: Docker Compose
description: Running several containers together.

name: Redis, caching and queues
description: In-memory caches, job queues and when a server needs them.

name: Build tooling
description: Vite, ESLint, npm scripts and package-lock.json.

name: In-browser machine learning
description: TensorFlow.js with a small open-source image model.

name: Publishing an npm package
description: Building a small shared library, publishing it and testing it with Jest.

name: Debugging
description: Reading errors, breakpoints, and code you wrote and code you did not. Mandatory: reading logs (on real devices) and isolating a bug (reproducing it).

name: Code review
description: Reading code critically, testing it and saying why it is right or wrong, including AI-written code.

name: Problem solving
description: JavaScript logic and approach: clarify, plan, think aloud, solve, verify and handle edge cases.

name: Communication
description: Explaining your work and decisions clearly, and answering behavioural questions in the STAR format.

name: System design basics
description: Reasoning about structure and trade-offs for a small system.

name: Ownership
description: Taking responsibility for outcomes, following through and learning from mistakes.

name: Agile and teamwork
description: Scrum basics, Jira, stand-ups and working well in a team.
